newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Afghan factions battle north of Kabul.
newsitem.headline: Afghan factions battle north of Kabul.

text.p: Afghan factions fighting over a strategic pass north of the capital Kabul exchanged occasional artillery fire early on Wednesday but the front was largely quiet.

A warplane belonging to the forces of northern Uzbek leader General Abdul Rashid Dostum bombed positions held by the Taleban militia on the De Sabz pass, around 30 km (20 miles) north of Kabul, at around 8.15 am (0345 GMT).
"It was quiet overnight," said a commander with former government forces in Kalakan, a village around 25 km (15 miles) north of the capital.
Dostum's forces, along with those of the ousted Afghan government, have been fighting for days to try to dislodge Taleban troops from the pass.

Forces loyal to the former government want to push the radical Islamic Taleban militia out of Kabul, which the group siezed at the end of last month. The Taleban now control over two thirds of the country.

A spokesman for the former government said its military commander, Ahmad Shah Masood, was in the northern town of Taloqan on Wednesday for talks with ousted president Burhanuddin Rabbani and former prime minister Gulbuddin Hekmatyar.
